Bill To: Locked Bill To, a user with only one of the two permissions

A user who has only ONE of the two permissions the PRD names clicks a locked Bill To field. Does the error message show its button ("Go To Invoice" or "Open Deposits") or not?
(a) The button needs BOTH permissions: a user missing either one gets the message with no button
(b) The button is hidden only when the user has NEITHER permission: one of the two is enough to see it
(c) Something else (please say)

S5-N1: "Without 'Invoicing & payments → View' and 'See Financial Data', the M4 toast shows with no button." S5-N2: "Without 'View and Manage AP/AR Data' and 'Customers → View', the M1 toast shows with no button." The sentences can be read as "missing both" or "missing either". (Elsewhere the PRD writes "or" when one missing permission is enough, S1-N2.) The cases for a user who has neither permission are written and runnable; only the one-of-two cases wait.
PRD v0.5 Story 5 (SV-12307), S5-N1 and S5-N2; S1-N2 for the "or" wording
Bill To: Credit Hold banner on an invoiced work order

If the work order's own customer is on Credit Hold (and the payer is not), does the banner show today's "This customer is on Credit Hold!" for the customer, or nothing?
(a) It shows today's banner for the customer ("This customer is on Credit Hold!"), because an invoiced work order reads as today
(b) It shows nothing, because the customer's Credit Hold does not matter when someone else is billed
(c) Something else (please say)

S7-N4: "Once invoiced, the banner reads as today." Today the banner describes the work order's customer. S7-N1: "The customer's own Credit Hold does not block when someone else is billed." S7-R11: "The work order's Credit Hold and Over Limit badges describe the Bill To." The PRD does not say whose Credit Hold the banner on an invoiced work order describes when the two customers differ.
PRD v0.5 Story 7 (SV-12309), S7-N1, S7-N4 and S7-R11
Bill To: Credit Hold and Over Limit badges on a part sale

When a part sale is billed to someone else, should its Credit Hold and Over Limit badges describe the payer, as the work order's badges do, or the part sale's own customer, as today?
(a) The payer, the same as on a work order
(b) The part sale's own customer, as today
(c) Something else (please say)

S7-R11: "The work order's Credit Hold and Over Limit badges describe the Bill To." The PRD says this for work orders only and is silent about the same badges on a part sale (Story 7 puts the part sale's Credit Hold banner on its Finance tab, S7-R6). The banner and invoicing already follow the payer on part sales, so a badge that kept describing the customer would contradict the banner.
PRD v0.5 Story 7 (SV-12309), S7-R6 and S7-R11
Bill To: Order of the Bill To list

When a work order already bills another customer and you open its Bill To list (for example with Change Bill To), where should the current Bill To appear?
(a) As the spec: the "(this customer)" row first, then every customer A to Z, the current Bill To in its A to Z place (as the customer windows do).
(b) As the design: the "(this customer)" row first, the current Bill To second, then the rest A to Z.
(c) Something else (please say).

The spec says "the first option is always "[customer] (this customer)"" and the list is A to Z. The design's page 3 pictures put the current Bill To second; its page 1 pictures (customer windows) keep the current pick in its A to Z place.

Spec: Story 3 (SV-12305), the Bill To search rule. The design "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), page "3 When the Bill To is blocked", pictures "Change Bill To" and "Phone, Change Bill To"; page 1, picture "Open" (Edit Customer).
Bill To: Close button on the locked Bill To message

When someone clicks a Bill To that cannot be changed, the design shows a red message with "Go To Invoice" (or "Open Deposits") AND a "Close" button; people who may not open the Finance or Deposits tab get the red message with only "Close". Which is right?
(a) As the design: red message, the action button when allowed, plus Close for everyone.
(b) As the spec: only the action button; people without it get the app's standard error message with the line "Please try to resolve this.", which fades after 3 seconds.
(c) Something else (please say).

The spec names one button ("Go To Invoice" / "Open Deposits") and says the others get the message "with no button"; its section 8 says messages without a button are the standard error message with "Please try to resolve this." that fades after 3 seconds, and messages with a button fade after 10 seconds.

Spec: Story 5 (SV-12307), the click rules and the 'no button' rules; section 8 (messages). The design "Bill To design" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2prSHgwt2tWCz96QD2DWkd), page 3, pictures "Click" (invoiced, deposit, mary.moore) and "Phone, tap".
